hook.text: Data is encrypted at rest and in transit. But what about during processing? Confidential computing protects data in use.

buildup.text: Secure enclaves (TEEs) isolate data during processing. Not even the cloud provider or OS can access it.

discovery.text: Intel SGX, AMD SEV, and ARM TrustZone provide hardware-level isolation. Cloud providers offer these as managed features.

twist.text: Confidential computing lets healthcare and finance use the cloud for sensitive data they couldn't process before.

climax.text: The Confidential Computing Consortium is standardizing the tech. Full lifecycle encryption is the new normal.

punchline.text: Encrypted while processing. Not even the cloud can see your data.

quiz.question: What does confidential computing protect against?
options: Unauthorized access to data while it's being actively processed in memory
Data breaches during file transfers between data centers
Physical theft of hard drives from data centers

details.summary: Confidential computing protects data while it is being processed, not just at rest or in transit, by using hardware-based trusted execution environments. This means cloud providers cannot access customer data even while their servers are computing on it.
details.whyItMatters: Confidential computing solves the last major trust barrier in cloud adoption. Organizations that could not trust cloud providers with sensitive data processing can now use the cloud securely.
takeaways: Data is encrypted even while being actively processed
Hardware-based protection prevents provider access to data
Regulated industries can migrate sensitive workloads to cloud

faq.question: How does confidential computing work?
faq.answer: Processors like Intel SGX, AMD SEV, and ARM CCA create hardware-enforced encrypted enclosures called trusted execution environments. Data is decrypted only inside the CPU, invisible to the operating system, hypervisor, and cloud provider. Even physical access to the server cannot expose the data.

faq.question: Who benefits most from confidential computing?
faq.answer: Healthcare organizations processing patient records, financial institutions handling transactions, government agencies with classified data, and any multi-party computation where participants do not fully trust each other.
